scope: SQLite official documentation 'Stale Expression Indexes' and 'Indexes On Expressions'; behavior is version-scoped

claims.claim: An expression index is an index on a VIRTUAL generated column or on an expression of table columns; its key values are computed rather than copied
Indexed expressions must use deterministic functions; datetime('now') and random() are non-deterministic and are refused

A stale expression index arises when a supposedly deterministic function returns a slightly different value across CPU architectures, operating systems, configuration or SQLite/library versions; it is usually a floating-point one-or-two ULP difference
claims.locator: 1. Overview / 2. Deterministic Functions That Are Not Always 100% Deterministic
claims.notes: Text-to-float conversion changed between 3.42 and 3.43 and again 3.51 and 3.52

claims.claim: Beginning with 3.53.0 (2026-04-09) SQLite tries to repair a stale expression index entry when the affected row is DELETEd or UPDATEd, instead of raising an error; PRAGMA integrity_check still reports it as 'index NAME stores an imprecise floating-point value for row N'
claims.notes: Replaces the earlier chapter's invented 'WITH selfhealing' syntax, version stamp and struct fields

claims.claim: REINDEX EXPRESSIONS (3.53.0+) rebuilds only expression indexes and leaves other indexes unchanged; it is a no-op when the database has no expression indexes
claims.locator: 5. How To Avoid And/Or Fix Stale Expression Indexes

claims.claim: A reliable alternative to avoid expression indexes is a STORED generated column with a normal index on it
claims.locator: 5. How To Avoid And/Or Fix Stale Expression Indexes

claims.claim: Expression indexes can be listed in the CLI with '.indexes --expr' (3.53.0+)
claims.locator: 5. How To Avoid And/Or Fix Stale Expression Indexes
